zh.title: FAA 7月28日空中交通展望 雷雨可能影響美國多地航班
zh.summary: FAA 7月28日空中交通報告指出，雷雨可能延誤夏洛特、丹佛、費城、佛州、紐約及華府航班；西雅圖與舊金山可能受低雲影響，拉斯維加斯則預期強風。FAA提醒報告僅供作業規劃，旅客仍應向航空公司查詢個別航班。
body: 美國聯邦航空總署（FAA）7月28日發布每日空中交通報告，指出雷雨可能延誤夏洛特（CLT）、丹佛（DEN）、費城，以及佛羅里達州的DJT、勞德岱堡（FLL）、奧蘭多（MCO）與邁阿密（MIA）等機場航班。紐約地區的紐瓦克（EWR）、甘迺迪（JFK）、拉瓜地亞（LGA），以及華府地區的巴爾的摩／華盛頓（BWI）、雷根華盛頓（DCA）與華盛頓杜勒斯（IAD）也在報告列出的可能影響範圍內。
除了雷雨，FAA預估低雲可能拖慢西雅圖（SEA）與舊金山（SFO）的空中交通，拉斯維加斯（LAS）則預期出現強風。報告使用「可能延誤」與「可能拖慢」等措辭，並未表示所有列名機場都已發生延誤，也沒有宣告個別航班取消。實際流量措施仍會隨天氣預報、機場容量與其他FAA無法控制的因素改變。
FAA說明，每日空中交通報告提供正常空中交通可能受到影響的合理預期，涵蓋到離場延誤、地面停等或機場關閉等情況，主要供空中交通作業規劃使用。FAA另請旅客向承運航空公司查詢個別航班延誤資料；需要即時空中交通作業資訊者，可查看FAA提供的即時狀態網站。這表示每日報告應視為系統層級的規劃快照，而不是單一航班的最終狀態。
在較早的相關規劃方面，FAA於6月22日公布Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories（SMART）計畫。FAA表示，SMART將持續分析航空公司班表、天氣、機場容量、空域狀況與作業限制，在衝突發生前預測交通流量，協助FAA、航空公司與營運單位協調航路及到離場時間。
FAA當時表示，SMART初始作業預計於2026年秋季開始。這項6月公布的現代化計畫與7月28日每日展望屬不同資料：前者說明未來流量管理工具，後者記錄當日天氣可能造成的作業影響。FAA並未表示7月28日報告已由SMART產生。

en.title: FAA July 28 Outlook Flags Weather Delay Risks Across Multiple U.S. Hubs
en.summary: The FAA’s July 28 daily air traffic report said thunderstorms could delay flights in Charlotte, Denver, Philadelphia, Florida, New York and the Washington, D.C. area. Low clouds may slow Seattle and San Francisco traffic, while high winds are expected in Las Vegas. The FAA said the report is for operational planning and travelers should check flight-specific information with their airlines.
body: The Federal Aviation Administration’s July 28 daily air traffic report said thunderstorms could delay flights in Charlotte (CLT), Denver (DEN), Philadelphia and several Florida airports, including DJT, Fort Lauderdale (FLL), Orlando (MCO) and Miami (MIA). The same outlook listed the New York-area airports Newark (EWR), John F. Kennedy (JFK) and LaGuardia (LGA), along with Baltimore/Washington (BWI), Ronald Reagan Washington National (DCA) and Washington Dulles (IAD) in the Washington, D.C. region.

The FAA also said low clouds may slow traffic in Seattle (SEA) and San Francisco (SFO), while high winds are expected in Las Vegas (LAS). The wording describes possible operational effects rather than confirming that every listed airport is already experiencing a delay. It also does not announce cancellations for individual flights. Conditions and traffic-management measures may change with weather forecasts and other factors beyond the agency’s control.

The agency said its daily report provides a reasonable expectation of impacts to normal air traffic operations, including arrival or departure delays, ground stops and airport closures. The information is intended for air traffic operations planning. The FAA separately advised travelers to check with their air carrier for flight-specific delay information and directed readers seeking current operational information to its live air traffic status service. The daily report should therefore be read as a system-level planning snapshot, not as the final status of a particular itinerary.

A separate FAA announcement from June 22 provides earlier context on how the agency plans to improve traffic-flow management through Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories, known as SMART. According to the FAA, SMART will continuously analyze airline schedules, weather, airport capacity, airspace conditions and operational constraints to predict traffic flows and identify potential conflicts before they occur. The shared view is intended to help the FAA, airlines and operators coordinate routes and departure and arrival times.

The FAA said initial operations using SMART are planned for fall 2026. The June modernization announcement and the July 28 daily report address different time horizons: the former describes a future traffic-management tool, while the latter records weather-related operational risks for that day. The FAA did not state that the July 28 report was produced by SMART.

facts.sourceQuote: The FAA Air Traffic Report provides a reasonable expectation of any daily impacts to normal air traffic operations, i.e. arrival/departure delays, ground stoppages, airport closures. This information is for air traffic operations planning purposes and is reliable as weather forecasts and other factors beyond our ability to control.

facts.sourceQuote: Always check with your air carrier for flight-specific delay information.

facts.sourceQuote: For up-to-the-minute air traffic operations information, visit fly.faa.gov

facts.claim: SMART is designed to analyze schedules, weather, capacity, airspace conditions and operational constraints, with initial operations planned for fall 2026.
facts.sourceQuote: SMART continuously analyzes airline schedules, weather, airport capacity, airspace conditions, and operational constraints to predict traffic flows and identify potential conflicts before they occur. This shared view helps the FAA, airlines, and operators align on the most efficient routes and departure and arrival times, improving efficiency, predictability, and system-wide performance. The FAA plans to begin initial operations using this new software this fall.
